components.name: Secondary Button

components.name: Live Chip

components.css: .ds-chip-live { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; font: 800 10.5px/1.6 'Public Sans', system-ui, sans-serif; letter-spacing: .1em; color: var(--rt-live, #FF4D63); border: 1px solid var(--rt-live-edge, rgba(255, 77, 99, .34)); background: var(--rt-live-tint, rgba(255, 77, 99, .10)); border-radius: 999px; padding: 2px 9px 2px 7px; } .ds-chip-dot { width: 7px; height: 7px; border-radius: 50%; background: var(--rt-live, #FF4D63); animation: ds-pulse 1.4s ease infinite; } @keyframes ds-pulse { 0%, 100% { box-shadow: 0 0 0 0 rgba(255, 77, 99, .34); } 55% { box-shadow: 0 0 0 5px rgba(255, 77, 99, 0); } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-chip-dot { animation: none; } }

components.name: Radio Card

components.css: .ds-radio { cursor: pointer; display: flex; gap: 12px; align-items: flex-start; padding: 12px 14px; width: 100%; text-align: left; border-radius: 10px; border: 1px solid var(--rt-line, #242D39); background: var(--rt-surface-2, #1C2430); color: var(--rt-ink, #EDF1F7); font: 400 13.5px/1.5 'Public Sans', system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-radio b { font-weight: 700; } .ds-radio-sub { display: block; color: var(--rt-ink-2, #9BA7B8); font-size: 12.5px; } .ds-radio-mark { width: 16px; height: 16px; flex: none; margin-top: 2px; border-radius: 50%; border: 1px solid var(--rt-line-strong, #38424F); background: var(--rt-surface, #141A22); } .ds-radio[aria-checked=true] { border-color: var(--rt-accent-edge, rgba(255, 157, 46, .34)); background: var(--rt-accent-tint, rgba(255, 157, 46, .10)); } .ds-radio[aria-checked=true] .ds-radio-mark { border: 5px solid var(--rt-accent, #FF9D2E); background: var(--rt-on-accent, #180D01); } .ds-radio:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--rt-focus, #FFC578); outline-offset: 2px; }

narrative.overview: A rail yard after dark: deep slate surfaces stacked like night air, and one warm sodium-vapor lamp (#FF9D2E) doing all the pointing. The system is dark by construction, not by inversion — five slate steps build depth tonally, hairline borders do the structure, and the sodium accent appears only where the product wants your hand: the primary button, the Live Link, the selected state. Everything operational — times, counts, URLs, stage labels — switches to DM Mono, like departure boards in a station. This system governs exactly two pages: configurator.html and index.html, which share the --rt-* token block in assets/app.css. Outside this system on purpose: preview.html keeps its older, dimmer palette, and the Overlay's Theme art is per-Theme, governed by docs/authoring-a-theme.md, never by these tokens.
keyCharacteristics: One warm accent (sodium orange) on tonal deep slate; every other hue is a status voice.
Public Sans for prose and UI; DM Mono for anything a machine would print.
Pill controls and pill badges; softly rounded cards (14px); hairline borders everywhere.
Checkerboard stages wherever OBS transparency is being depicted.
Transform-only, slow motion — the OBS performance mandate reaches the app's own chrome.

rules.name: The One Lamp Rule
rules.body: Sodium is the only hue that means "act here" or "this is chosen." Every other color is a status report, never a call to action.

rules.name: The Tint-and-Edge Rule
rules.body: A colored surface is never a solid flood: it is the hue's -tint fill paired with its -edge border. Solid status color is reserved for dots, text, and the accent button itself.

rules.name: The Ink Floor Rule
rules.body: Helper copy below 14px reads in ink-2 — ink-3 sits under the 4.5:1 contrast floor at that size and is reserved for large or non-essential marks.

rules.name: The Timetable Rule
rules.body: Anything a machine would print — a time, a count, a URL, a slug, a stage label — is DM Mono. Anything a person would say is Public Sans. No third font.

rules.name: The Sodium Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: Sections are introduced by the uppercase sodium micro-label, not by big headings. The heading below it stays sentence-case and tight.

rules.name: The minmax(0,1fr) Rule
rules.body: Every fluid grid track is minmax(0, 1fr) and every flex/grid child that can carry text gets min-width: 0 — the Live Link URL and a Twitch login are single unbreakable words. Rail widths are modifier classes, never inline styles.

rules.name: The Earned Glow Rule
rules.body: The sodium glow marks the one thing a screen most wants you to do or the thing you chose — never decoration. If two elements on a screen glow sodium, one of them is lying.

rules.name: The Checkerboard Rule
rules.body: Anywhere the UI depicts what OBS will composite, the stage is a dark checkerboard (~22-28px squares, near-invisible contrast) with a mono uppercase stage label in ink-3.

dos: Do style with --rt-* tokens; the legacy aliases (--bg, --gold, …) exist only so old markup reskins.
Do ship every new status color as the full trio: solid + -tint (~10%) + -edge (~30%).
Do set anything machine-printed in DM Mono with tabular-nums, uppercase and letter-spaced when it labels.
Do wrap fluid columns in minmax(0, 1fr) and give their children min-width: 0 — assume every string might be one unbreakable word.
Do animate with transform/opacity only, on slow timers, and honor prefers-reduced-motion on every animation.
Do keep new-page layout in that page's own inline <style>; assets/app.css is a shared vocabulary, not a framework.
donts: Don't put white text on sodium — text on the accent is on-sodium (#180D01).
Don't glow more than one sodium element per screen, or glow anything that isn't the primary action or the chosen thing.
Don't use ink-3 for helper copy under 14px (contrast floor); it is for large or non-essential marks only.
Don't add Unicode-glyph or icon-font icons; draw them as inline stroke SVG in currentColor.
Don't extend these tokens into preview.html (its palette diverges on purpose) or into Theme art (per-Theme, see docs/authoring-a-theme.md).
Don't revive the pre-v2 blue/gold (#57b6ff / #f4c430); the sodium system replaced it app-wide.
